scope: Theorem 6.3 (One-slot bounds with the sharp coefficient) of the manuscript “Bloch's Law for Finite-Range Heisenberg Ferromagnets in Three Dimensions” (preprints/Blochs-Law-for-Finite-Range-Heisenberg-Ferromagnets-in-Three-Dimensions-October-5-2026/bloch-law-heisenberg.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 271 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 4884bc0984dfd0f6), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 33. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is a constant C < ∞, independent of K, with the following property. For every integer K ≥ 1 there are βK < ∞ and a nonnegative function ϵK(β) → 0 as β → ∞, such that for β ≥ βK, every finite cube, every allowed pin set E, and every deterministic slot-time point i, dE(i) ≤ β−3/2 κ ℓ 2K−1 X n=1 n−3/2 + CK−1/2 + ϵK(β) ! . (6.14) If the site x of i additionally satisfies BRK (x̄) ⊆ Λ◦ , E has no pin over BRK (x̄), (6.15) then dE(i) ≥ β−3/2 κ ℓ K X n=1 n−3/2 − ϵK(β) ! . (6.16) For i / ∈ E, the same two bounds hold for r(E, {i}), with the same choice of error function. The threshold and error function are independent of the cube, cut, slot, and number, locations, and times of all finite extra pins. Only the fixed model and geometric choices, and K, may affect them.
